links.title: BIP 173: Base32 address format for native v0-16 witness outputs (status: Deployed)
links.why: Bech32 defined: the character set, the human-readable part, the separator and the checksum, with the test vectors this chapter reproduces.

links.title: BIP 350: Bech32m format for v1+ witness addresses (status: Deployed)
links.why: What bech32m changed and why: the single constant that removes the length-extension weakness bech32 had, which this chapter demonstrates.

links.title: BIP 340: Schnorr Signatures for secp256k1 (status: Deployed)
links.why: The signature scheme behind a taproot address, and the x-only public key it uses; the standard behind this chapter's newest address type.

links.title: BIP 86: Key Derivation for Single Key P2TR Outputs (status: Deployed)
links.why: The derivation and the tweak that turn a public key into a taproot output key, with the vector this chapter checks its own taproot address against.

links.title: libsecp256k1 (Bitcoin Core's elliptic-curve library)
links.why: The library the real software uses for the curve arithmetic this chapter performs in Python, and its own account of what it guarantees.

links.title: SEC 1: Elliptic Curve Cryptography (version 2.0)
links.why: Where the compressed and uncompressed point encodings come from, with the 02, 03 and 04 prefixes this chapter uses.

links.title: FIPS 180-4: Secure Hash Standard
links.why: The definition of SHA-256 itself, for a student who wants to see that the hash function this chapter calls is a published algorithm rather than a black box.

links.title: Base58Check encoding - Bitcoin Wiki
links.why: The older encoding step by step, including the version byte and the four-byte checksum this chapter recomputes.

links.title: Wallet import format - Bitcoin Wiki
links.why: How a private key is written for export, and what the trailing 01 of the compressed form means.

links.title: Invoice address - Bitcoin Wiki
links.why: The address types side by side with their prefixes and lengths, a useful table while reading this chapter's three address branches.

links.title: Elliptic Curve Digital Signature Algorithm - Bitcoin Wiki
links.why: The signature scheme that preceded Schnorr, still behind most spending; the background to this chapter's digital-signature concept.

links.title: BIP 173: Bech32 addresses
links.why: The format of native SegWit addresses.

links.title: Transactions (Developer Guide)
links.why: How the locking and unlocking scripts of this chapter are actually evaluated when an output is spent.

links.title: Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs) v1.0
links.why: The identifier standard this chapter's Semantics branch compares a Bitcoin address with: both name a subject by a key the subject controls.

links.title: Mastering Bitcoin, chapter 4 (source text)
links.why: The chapter this deck follows.

links.title: Diffie and Hellman: New Directions (PDF)
links.why: The 1976 paper behind the key pair.

links.title: base58.h in bitcoin/bitcoin (source)
links.why: Satoshi's four reasons, in the code.

links.title: BIP 350: Bech32m addresses
links.why: The fix used from witness version 1.

links.title: The eater address on blockstream.info
links.why: Open it and watch nothing move.

links.title: Bitcoin Wiki: technical background of addresses
links.why: From key to address, in steps.

links.why: Ask a question, read the answers.

links.why: The curve behind every public key, explained on screen
